findings.claim: The close X is located geometrically because the node order differs between the overlay variant (ImageView after the chip) and the app variant (ImageView before the chip). The new rule picks the topmost blank ImageView and, within that row, the rightmost, which matches both observed trees where the X sits in the header row and every other icon sits below it. Residual risk: an unobserved layout with a blank ImageView above the header would be picked instead; the log line listing every candidate with top and right bounds makes that diagnosable from logcat in one glance.

findings.claim: Non-Cruz-Verde detection reuses servicio, which only matches a non-address node containing cruz verde. The 0.5 s re-check gives the popup time to render that node and skips the close when it appears, which removes the premature-close race. Residual risk: a Picap render slower than 0.5 s whose only Cruz Verde text is an address would still be closed as non-CV. The NO-CV log lines make any misclassification visible in logcat.

findings.claim: The close action is unconditional per the explicit request: non-CV popups are dismissed even when the Picap auto-accept master switch is off. No data is registered and no accept click happens, so nothing irreversible occurs, but if browsing non-CV offers becomes desirable the branch will need a switch guard.

findings.claim: pendingCloseId deduplicates timers so concurrent events schedule one close attempt per order id, and lastClosedId is set only on a successful click, so a failed click retries on the next event with a fresh 0.5 s window (bounded by popup lifetime). Residual case: a click that reports success while the popup fails to close leaves the offer open with no automatic retry, until the user dismisses it manually.
